title: A 2026 crossover trial found caffeine + L-theanine did nothing extra for strength or endurance. So is focus the only real case for the stack?
text:
A crossover trial in competitive athletes this year tested caffeine alone, theanine alone and the two together on maximal strength, intermittent endurance and eye-hand coordination. The combination didn't beat caffeine on its own for physical output.

That lines up with how I've always thought about the stack. The older trials that made it popular (2008 and 2010) were about attention and task switching, not lifting more. The 2:1 theanine to caffeine ratio people quote comes from those.

So for people here who use it daily: is it the focus you notice, or mainly that the coffee jitters and the afternoon drop are smaller? And what ratio and timing settled in for you after a few months?

(Disclosure: I run a small supplement company, so weigh my take accordingly. No products or links in this post.)
